verdict.rationale: Elastic documents its own alerting rules: threshold rules on log aggregations, rules at service, environment and transaction level, and custom KQL queries. Alerts can send notifications to external services or third-party incident management systems, which is a thin form of routing. There is no evidence of grouping or silencing alert notifications; the error grouping in APM concerns stack traces, not alerts. Missing for 10: documented alert grouping/deduplication, silencing/muting/maintenance windows, explicit notification routing rules, coverage of all signal types (metrics, traces, SLO burn), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can alert on any telemetry signal with routing, grouping, and silencing of notifications

citations.quote: You can create a rule to send an alert when the log aggregation exceeds a threshold.
You can define rules at different levels (service, environment, transaction) or use custom KQL queries.
You can also extend your alerts with notifications via services or third-party incident management systems.
